title: fanoutqa: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations. (ca085ff48e269f74)

chat_history.content: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations.

content.content:
User wants list of US presidents who served two terms and their political party affiliation. Need to provide comprehensive list. Should include all presidents who served two full terms (or two terms, could be non-consecutive? Typically two terms means served two elected terms, could be non-consecutive like Grover Cleveland served two terms but not consecutively; still qualifies). Provide list with party affiliation. Should be up to date as of 2025. Include presidents who served two full terms (including those who died early in second term? Probably not). Provide list: Washington (None/No party), Jefferson (Democratic-Republican), Madison (Democratic-Republican), Monroe (Democratic-Republican), Jackson (Democratic), Van Buren? No, one term. Lincoln (Republican) served second term but assassinated early; still counts as two-term president? He was elected to second term but died. Usually considered two-term president. Similarly, Woodrow Wilson (Democratic), Dwight D. Eisenhower (Republican), Ronald Reagan (Republican), Bill Clinton (Democratic), George W. Bush (Republican), Barack Obama (Democratic), Donald Trump? only one term. So also include: Ulysses S. Grant? He served two terms (Republican). Also: James Madison? Already. James Monroe. James Monroe. Also: James K. Polk only one term. Andrew Jackson two terms. Martin Van Buren one. William Henry Harrison died early. John Quincy Adams one. James Buchanan one. Theodore Roosevelt succeeded after McKinley and then one term elected. So list: Washington (No party), Jefferson (Democratic-Republican), Madison (Democratic-Republican), Monroe (Democratic-Republican), Jackson (Democratic), Van Buren no, Grant (Republican), Cleveland (Democratic) - non-consecutive two terms, but qualifies as two terms. Also: McKinley assassinated early second term, but elected to second term. He served part of second term; still counts as two-term? Usually considered two-term president? Actually McKinley served one full term and part of second before assassination, but he's considered a two-term president (elected twice). So include him. Similarly, Lincoln. Also: Wilson, Eisenhower, Reagan, Clinton, Bush, Obama. Also: Franklin D. Roosevelt served four terms, qualifies as more than two but also two terms? He served more, but still served at least two terms; but the question likely wants presidents who served exactly two terms. Usually "served two terms" includes those who served two full terms, not more. So exclude FDR (four terms) and Washington (no party). Also exclude those who served more than two. So list those with exactly two terms.

Thus list: Washington (no party) - but served two terms, but no affiliation. Jefferson, Madison, Monroe, Jackson, Grant, Cleveland (non-consecutive), McKinley (partial second term?), Lincoln (partial), Wilson (full two), Eisenhower, Reagan, Clinton, Bush, Obama.

But need clarity. Provide table with name, term years, party.

Probably best to list all presidents who were elected to two terms (including non-consecutive) and note party. Exclude those who served more than two terms (FDR). Provide note about partial terms.

Let's produce answer.

content:
Below is a concise reference of every U.S. President who was **elected to two separate terms** (including the two‑term, non‑consecutive case of Grover Cleveland).  
For each president I list the party under which he ran, the years he held office, and a brief note on whether both terms were completed in full.

| # | President | Party (as elected) | Term(s) in Office | Full‑term?* |
|---|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|------------|
| 1 | **George Washington** | No formal party (Federalist‑leaning) | 1789‑1797 | Yes (two full 4‑year terms) |
| 2 | **Thomas Jefferson** | Democratic‑Republican | 1801‑1809 | Yes |
| 3 | **James Madison** | Democratic‑Republican | 1809‑1817 | Yes |
| 4 | **James Monroe** | Democratic‑Republican | 1817‑1825 | Yes |
| 5 | **Andrew Jackson** | Democratic | 1829‑1837 | Yes |
| 6 | **Ulysses S. Grant** | Republican | 1869‑1877 | Yes |
| 7 | **Grover Cleveland** | Democratic (non‑consecutive) | 1885‑1889 & 1893‑1897 | Yes (two full terms, separated by one term of Benjamin Harrison) |
| 8 | **William McKinley** | Republican | 1897‑1901 (assassinated early in 2nd term) | **No** – died 6 months into second term |
| 9 | **Theodore Roosevelt** – *not listed* (served only one elected term; succeeded after McKinley) |
|10| **Woodrow Wilson** | Democratic | 1913‑1921 | Yes |
|11| **Franklin D. Roosevelt** – *excluded* (served four terms, >2) |
|12| **Dwight D. Eisenhower** | Republican | 1953‑1961 | Yes |
|13| **Ronald Reagan** | Republican | 1981‑1989 | Yes |
|14| **Bill Clinton** | Democratic | 1993‑2001 | Yes |
|15| **George W. Bush** | Republican | 2001‑2009 | Yes |
|16| **Barack Obama** | Democratic | 2009‑2017 | Yes |

\* **Full‑term?** indicates whether the president completed the entire second four‑year term.  
- Presidents who died, resigned, or were removed during their second term (e.g., **William McKinley**, **Abraham Lincoln**) are marked “No.”  
- All others served the full eight years.

### Quick‑Reference Summary (Party‑Only)

| Party | Presidents who served two elected terms (incl. non‑consecutive) |
|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| **None / No party** | George Washington |
| **Democratic‑Republican** | Thomas Jefferson, James Madison, James Monroe |
| **Democratic** | Andrew Jackson, Grover Cleveland, Woodrow Wilson, Bill Clinton, Barack Obama |
| **Republican** | Ulysses S. Grant, William McKinley, Dwight D. Eisenhower, Ronald Reagan, George W. Bush |

> **Note:** If you are interested in presidents who served *exactly* two full terms (i.e., completed both eight years), omit William McKinley (assassinated) and Abraham Lincoln (assassinated). All other listed presidents meet that stricter criterion.
